summary.text: 菜 is a phonosemantic character for edible plants: 艸 marks the plant category, while 采 supplies a sound cue. It is also used for prepared food or dishes; the history and chronology of that sense are only partly established.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 艸 contributes the plant meaning category, and 采 supplies the pronunciation cue. The Shuowen definition identifies the referent as edible plants; a separate proposal derives the word from 采, “gather, pluck,” plus a nominal suffix, but that lexical derivation is not established by the graphic analysis.

components.text: 艹 is the conventional top-side form of 艸, the plant element in this character. Its role is semantic: it marks the category of vegetation, rather than depicting a plant in a scene.
采 is the sound-bearing component. Its own earlier graphic analysis is a hand picking from a tree or fruit; that pictorial origin belongs to 采 and does not make it a picture of 菜’s referent.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 菜 *sʰɯːs and 采 *sʰɯːʔ share the onset and rhyme; 菜 has an added departing-tone suffix. Modern Mandarin cài and cǎi retain a related initial and rhyme but differ in tone. Reconstructions are model-based, not recorded pronunciations.

history.text: The curated seal-script-style image presents the 艸-plus-采 analysis, but it is a modern redraw in the Shuowen tradition, not an ancient specimen. The consulted inventory reports bronze forms and a slip-text example, but their dates and earliest secure attestation of the full graph remain unclear; no secure oracle-bone form of 菜 is established here.

Qin slips are reported to write the vegetable word in 采羹, and Han examples also use 采 for 菜. This is an earlier spelling practice; it does not show that the graph 菜 originated from 采. Some proposed early bronze and Chu examples with a 采-like element have disputed readings.

uncertainties.text: The proposed word history “what is gathered or plucked,” from 采 plus a nominal suffix, is a scholarly derivation, not a result proved by the character’s 艸-plus-采 structure. The consulted research did not establish that proposal independently.

The evidence supports both vegetable and prepared-food senses, but does not provide a comprehensive dated Chinese chronology connecting them. Japanese examples date particular uses, not the origin of the character or the native reading な.

senses.period: Han dictionary definition; Qin-period spelling evidence
senses.text: The Shuowen definition identifies 菜 as edible vegetation. Qin slips reportedly write the vegetable word with 采; this supports the word’s use but does not date the first appearance of the full graph 菜.

senses.period: Qin-period example; later Chinese use; Japanese example dated approximately 1120
senses.text: 菜 is also used for prepared food or a dish. Qin 采羹 is reported as 菜羹, and a later Chinese use for prepared food is noted; the evidence here does not establish a full sequence from vegetables to dishes. Japanese sources separately cite a side-dish sense around 1120.
Modern glosses include vegetables and dishes or food. The supplied definitions do not establish that every gloss represents a distinct, chronologically ordered sense.

developments.text: Both senses are attested in the supplied account, but the evidence does not establish when or by what path the food or dish sense developed from edible vegetation.

limitations.text: The earliest secure attestation of the full graph 菜 and a comprehensive dated Chinese sense history remain unresolved in the consulted material.
A proposal connects the word 菜 to 采 “gather, pluck” plus a nominal suffix, but the source material does not establish it as the historical semantic development.

overview.text: 菜 names edible plants and vegetables. 艹 marks the plant category, while 采 provides a sound cue; the character is also used for dishes or prepared food.

components.text: 艹 marks the plant category. It is the side form of 艸 in this character.
采 supplies the sound cue. Its own hand-and-tree picture belongs to its earlier graphic history.

relationships.text: 艹, the side form of 艸, marks the plant category in 菜.
采 supplies the sound cue in 菜; the Shuowen parsing and compatible Zhengzhang reconstructions support this role.
